messages:
marta: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need to decide how the validator mesh should shard routing decisions for new model admissions. High-level tradeoffs: centralized router vs. distributed per-prober routing.

devin: central router = simpler telemetry and global dedupe, but single logical bottleneck and more ops overhead for HA.

alyssa: distributed per-prober sounds nicer for scale, but we lose easy global view for golden coverage. How do we ensure two probers don't duplicate expensive bench runs? :thinking:

marta: Right. One idea: keep distributed routing, but add a small coordination layer that leases "golden slots" for a model id. Lease service is cheap (<5ms) and only used for golden/growth probes.

sam: +1 on leases. Also we should make the default behavior optimistic: if no lease present, probe locally but mark results as provisional until a golden pass completes.

kevin: Operational question — how long are leases? We should avoid long locks that block reingestion. Suggest 30s default with backoff for retries.

alyssa: 30s seems ok. Also need to think about sample stratification across shards: heavy tail models (long seq + large batch) should go to bench machines with larger GPU mem. Routing needs to be size-aware.

marta: Agreed. Proposed routing keys: model_id + max_seq + estimated_params_bin. That lets us deterministically map to shard pools.

devin: For compatibility checks we also need to enforce runtime ABI constraints (kv cache shape, past-kv layout). We could encode an "abi_hash" that the router uses to find compatible validators.

sam: We already compute model fingerprints during ingest. Extend that fingerprint with an abi_hash field. Router matching becomes a set intersection: fingerprint.abi_hash in pool.supported_abis.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary pool autoscaler at 10->50 ramp will be triggered on router config change. Please coordinate with eng-infra.

marta: Good catch infra-bot. We'll gate config change behind a small canary rollout and manual signoff from infra.

kevin: On the bench-side, we need to prevent duplicate heavy runs. Suggest we add a short-lived cache keyed by (model_id, bench_profile) with TTL=5m and a small jitter to avoid stampedes.

alyssa: That handles duplicates but not replays for different commit hashes. Bench_profile should include model_binary_digest and quantization_tag.

devin: For fallback behavior: if routing cannot find a compatible pool, router should fallback to a small software-simulated smoke run on CPU to catch immediate rejects (fast failure) and mark model as "needs envoy" for a full bench.

marta: Yes — and put a higher priority queue for fast-fail smoke jobs so they don't wait behind long benches. We want fast feedback to model owners.

sam: UX: model owners get a short report link immediately. Report includes status: provisional/golden/failed + basic perf numbers. Use same URL scheme as current ingest: /models/<id>/admit-report

kevin: Implementation notes:
```
router.matching_keys = ["model_id", "max_seq", "param_bin", "abi_hash"]
lease_service.acquire(model_id, role="golden", ttl=30s)
bench_cache.set((model_id, bench_profile), result, ttl=300s)
```

alyssa: Testing plan: unit tests for router key derivation, integration test with 3 shard pools (small/medium/large), chaos test where lease service becomes slow.

marta: Action items:
- devin: prototype lease service + API doc (due EOW)
- sam: bench cache PR + TTL config (due Wed)
- alyssa: integration tests matrix and smoke-run fallback harness (due Fri)
- kevin: coord with eng-infra for canary rollout plan (sync by tomorrow)

devin: I'll post a short design doc with API surface and lease semantics after this thread.

marta: Thanks all. If no objections I'll open an RFC follow-up that captures these decisions and the rollout checklist.

alyssa: No objections from me. :thumbsup:

sam: SGTM.

kevin: Fine by me.

marta: Closing loop — ping me in-thread if infra-bot surfaces any deploy alerts during canary.
